0.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type X (GSD X) is caused by a deficiency in the enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase, specifically the muscle isoform encoded by the PGAM2 gene. This enzyme plays a crucial role in glycolysis by catalyzing the interconversion of 3-phosphoglycerate and 2-phosphoglycerate. A deficiency in muscle-specific phosphoglycerate mutase compromises the glycolytic pathway in muscle tissue, leading to reduced ATP production during exercise. As a result, individuals with GSD X experience exercise intolerance and muscle cramps due to the inability to properly utilize glycogen stores for energy.
